articles.name: Release notes through 2026-10-02
articles.title: Release notes through 2026-10-02
articles.body:
See the What's New section for an overview of last month's releases.

This week's release notes include:

  • Knowledge
  • AI Agents
  • Contact Center
  • Mobile SDKs
  • App Marketplace
  • Products with no updates this week

Knowledge

New

  • Knowledge
    • Knowledge context panel search filters are more flexible. The filter menu no longer limits the number of default filters you can apply. The external source dropdown loads all sources with pagination, and selected filter tags collapse into a compact, two-row summary.

Fixed

  • Knowledge
    • Links in generative search answers, including Quick Answers, now work as clickable links.
    • Badge names and categories in the award badge modal now wrap fully and stay visible when custom text spacing is applied.
  • Knowledge Creations
    • Community Content Moderation now refreshes a stale CSRF token and retries once after a 403 error. This happens when an admin re-authenticates from a moderation email, so the action no longer stops.

AI Agents

New

  • AI Agents Insights
    • AI-guided agent onboarding is rolling out to all eligible AI Agents customers through October. The updated onboarding detects topics from ticket history, generates context-matched procedures and knowledge articles in one click, and runs automated tests to assess agent readiness. See Creating an AI agent to automatically resolve customer issues for details.
  • AIAA
    • Segments in Procedures for email AI agents with agentic AI were released on September 28, 2026.
    • The Essential AI Agent Self-service Migration tool has been available to all Essential AI Agent customers since September 30, 2026.
    • The Ask for Details dialog builder node has been available to all AI Agent customers since September 30, 2026. It lets AI agents collect structured information from customers during conversations.
    • Configurable Knowledge and Welcome replies launched for email AI agents with agentic AI. See System replies in email AI agents.
  • Procedure Editor
    • Procedure sources are easier to scan. Long source titles now truncate cleanly, ticket IDs no longer clutter source names, and icons and spacing are more consistent.

Fixed

  • Procedure Editor
    • Fixed an issue where slow-loading recommendations could leave the side panel showing a loading state or make the recommendations list appear empty.

Contact Center

New

  • Contact Center
    • Outbound queue selection is now available in Contact Center. Admins can let agents choose an outbound queue before placing a call to control the caller ID and Amazon Connect flow. This improves routing consistency and brings feature parity with the legacy experience. For more information, see Configuring outbound queue selection.

Fixed

  • Contact Center
    • Improved the voicemail admin experience by fixing truncated and untranslated notifications, aligning dropdown controls, and correcting alert spacing.

Mobile SDKs

New

  • iOS version 2.41.0
    • Added brand filtering to keep conversations, real-time updates, login requests, and push notification navigation within the active brand.
    • Added support for Serbian.
    • Added VoiceOver announcements for sent-message status and agent typing.
    • Added Dynamic Type support for conversation headers.
    • Added support for custom locale selection through Zendesk.initialize. The selected locale is applied to the SDK UI and backend communication.
  • Android version 3.1.0
    • Brand filtering: When enabled in Zendesk settings, brand filtering applies to conversations, real-time updates, and push notifications.
    • App language: The SDK follows the language selected in the app. If the SDK doesn't support that language, it uses the default language.

Fixed

  • iOS version 2.41.0
    • Fixed an issue with push notification token updates.
    • Fixed crashes that could occur while setting up or shutting down a connection.
    • Fixed device metadata reporting the SDK version instead of the host app version.
    • Fixed an empty overlay that remained after the keyboard was dismissed.
    • Fixed the connection banner being clipped at large text sizes.
    • Fixed message cells not being recalculated correctly after a system font size change.
  • Android version 3.1.0
    • Messaging navigation: Calling showMessaging while messaging is already open now takes users to the requested screen.
    • Authentication: Fixed an issue where a repeatedly rejected JWT could cause the SDK to retry authentication indefinitely.

App Marketplace

New:
  • Shipped.ai (Messaging)
    • Shipped.ai is an AI support agent built specifically for ecommerce. It does not just answer the question and hand off. It resolves the ticket like applying the promo code, filing the warranty claim, editing the order, creating the return, then confirming it back to the customer in the same conversation.
  • Schedule Send by Saasly (Support)
    • Schedule Send by Saasly allows support agents to compose replies in advance and automatically send them at a specific date and time. The app helps teams manage follow-ups, respond during business hours, and maintain consistent customer communication without manual reminders. 
  • Google + Meta Ads Conversion Tracking (Support) (paid)
    • Google + Meta Ads Conversion Tracking closes the loop between an ad click and the customer it produced. A Zendesk trigger tells it when an outcome happens - an order won, a signup, a completed job - and it reports that to Google Ads and Meta as a conversion, so your campaigns optimize toward real customers, not clicks.
  • Required Fields Manager (Support)
    • Required Fields Manager lets admins make any custom ticket field required to fill in, for any combination of ticket type and ticket status. This app lets Questions, Incidents, Problems, and Tasks each have their own rules for every status a ticket can be in — New, Open, Pending, On-hold, and Solved.
  • Stripe by Canadesk (Support)
    • Stripe by Canadesk gives you access to Stripe information directly on Zendesk tickets.  Open a ticket and the sidebar looks the requester up in Stripe by email address, then shows information around your customers' Stripe subscription, payments, invoices, and their customer record.  Perform actions from Stripe like refunding a card payment, cancel a subscription at the end of a period, end a subscription immediately, or copy the customers billing portal link in a reply.
  • CRM Scene Customer Context (Support)
    • CRM Scene Customer Context helps agents understand the person behind a ticket. See customer contact details, the organization shown on the ticket, previous tickets, and things that may need attention without leaving Zendesk Support. 
  • Pulse (Support)
    • Pulse shows the event history of a ticket requester or a user profile, right in the sidebar. It highlights activity that happens outside of Zendesk — purchases, logins, phone calls, cancellations — alongside native Zendesk events, so agents don't have to piece together context from multiple systems.
  • Auto Internal Note (Support)
    • Auto Internal Note gives agents a rich-text workspace in the ticket sidebar for drafting internal context while they work. When the ticket status changes or the ticket is saved, the app waits briefly, posts the content as a private internal note, and clears the editor after a successful post.
  • Qualtrics Task (Support)
    • Qualtrics Task ets Qualtrics customers turn survey responses and workflow events into Zendesk activity. After an administrator connects a Zendesk account, actions added to a Qualtrics survey or workflow can create or update Zendesk profiles, records, and tickets using data collected in Qualtrics. For example, you can flag a low NPS rating to your Customer Success team, or let respondents reach out to your support team directly from a survey.
  • Outreach (Support)
    • Outreach puts a proactive ticket composer in the Zendesk Support navigation bar. Pick the people, write the ticket once, personalize it with placeholders, and Outreach creates one ticket per person through Zendesk's own bulk API, with live progress and a per-person result.
  • Change Manager (Support)
    • Change Manager adds a fifth ticket type, Change, next to Question, Incident, Problem and Task. Pick Change, choose a change type such as Emergency, Normal or Standard, and the ticket shows exactly the fields that kind of change needs: reason for change, risk, implementation and backout plans, or whatever fields you choose. Every other change field stays out of the way.
  • Power Views (Support)
    • Power Views is an alternative to the built-in views page. Organize views into folders, edit them live and watch the results change as you type, and bulk edit anything from two tickets to the whole view.
  • Employee Onboarding (Support)
    • Employee Onboarding adds a new employee form to the Zendesk Support navigation bar. Fill it in and the app creates a ticket for the new hire: they become the requester, get a friendly welcome message straight away, and the ticket holds everything your team needs to get them ready for day one.
  • Customer Notes (Support)
    • Customer Notes puts a living profile of the customer next to every ticket. Agents write notes about the person, not the ticket, tag them with traits like VIP or Do not call, and see their history and health at a glance.
  • Project Manager (Support)
    • Project Manager turns tickets into projects. A project is a ticket, and every task in it is a ticket too, so the work is assigned, tracked and reported on like everything else in Zendesk. See the whole project as a tree, re-arrange it by drag and drop, and see the plan on a Gantt chart right beside it.
  • Chatbase WhatsApp Relay (Support)
    • Chatbase WhatsApp Relay is the companion app for the Chatbase WhatsApp relay. When your Chatbase AI agent escalates a WhatsApp conversation to Zendesk, agents reply from the ticket and Chatbase delivers those replies back to the customer on WhatsApp.

Products with no updates this week

  • Support
  • Chat and messaging
  • AI/Copilot
  • Analytics
  • Talk
  • Admin Center
  • Quality assurance
  • Workforce management

articles.name: Workflow: Re-assign tickets without a group after 1 hour
articles.title: Workflow: Re-assign tickets without a group after 1 hour
articles.body:
If a ticket remains unassigned to a group for more than an hour, I'd like to create an automation to assign it to a default group. Also, how can I exclude AI agents from the conditions for those tickets?

The workflow includes the steps below.

Step 1: Check for ticket tags

First, ensure that your AI agent workflow adds this dedicated tag to tickets: handled_by_ai_agent. Add that tag immediately through the AI integration.

Step 2: Create a fallback automation

Create a fallback automation with at least four Meet all conditions:

  • Ticket: Group | Is | -
  • Ticket: Status category | Less than | Solved
  • Ticket: Hours since created | Greater than | 1

  • Ticket: Tags | Contains none of the following | handled_by_ai_agent auto_assigned_default_group

Step 3: Add actions

In your automation, add the following actions:

  • Ticket: Group | select your default group

  • Ticket: Add tags | auto_assigned_default_group

Step 4: Create a test ticket

After 1 to 2 hours, verify that the automation appears in the events. This gives enough time for the automation to run.

articles.name: How can I use Google Sheets actions in action flows to search more than 5,000 rows?
articles.title: How can I use Google Sheets actions in action flows to search more than 5,000 rows?
articles.body:
Question

Can I use the Google Sheets Search rows action in action flows if it returns more than 5,000 rows?

Answer

Yes, you can configure the Google Sheets Search rows action to search the content of sheets with more than 5,000 rows. To achieve this, you must increase the row count.

How to increase the row count returned per page on Search rows

  1. In Admin Center, click Apps and integrations in the sidebar, then select Actions > Action flows.
  2. Click the name of an existing action flow to open it or click Create flow to create a new action flow.
  3. In the action builder, click the Add step icon ().
  4. In the step sidebar, under Connected, click Google Sheets and then select Search rows.
  5. Configure the step.
  6. Under Additional fields, select Row count and enter 5000. The row count value determines how many rows can be returned on the first page.
  7. If there are more than 5,000 search results, use the Page token returned in the response to retrieve the next page of results.
  8. Finish creating or updating the action flow as needed, and then click Save.

For more information, see these articles:

  • Creating action flows
  • Using Google Sheet actions in action flows

articles.name: Service Incident - September 21, 2026 - Support | All Pods - Multiple customers in the DACH region are seeing SMTP 554 rejections when sending ticket replies
articles.title: Service Incident - September 21, 2026 - Support | All Pods - Multiple customers in the DACH region are seeing SMTP 554 rejections when sending ticket replies
articles.body:
Summary

Between 07:50 UTC and 14:30 UTC on 21 September 2026, Support customers in the DACH region experienced delivery failures when sending outbound ticket replies to recipients using GMX, web.de, IONOS/1&1, and mail.com email addresses. Affected messages received permanent SMTP 554 rejection responses and were neither delivered nor automatically retried.

Timeline

September 21, 2026 14:09 UTC | September 21, 2026 7:09 AM PT

We are aware of an issue impacting outbound email delivery to some mail providers. Some outbound email may fail with an error code 554 -- permanent rejection, meaning the outbound email was not sent and will not be retried. We are working with these mail providers and will provide an update as soon as possible.

September 21, 2026 14:50 UTC | September 21, 2026 7:50 AM PT

We have observed recovery and are now seeing successful outbound email delivery to the affected email providers. Please let us know if you continue to see any 554 status coded rejections to these recipients. Unfortunately we are unable to resend these emails on your behalf, and we apologize for that inconvenience.

September 21, 2026 15:01 UTC | September 21, 2026 8:01 AM PT

We are no longer seeing any email rejections to the providers that were rejecting emails sent via Zendesk. We do apologize for the disruption in your ability to send outbound mail during this incident. You will find any failed outbound emails in each of the respective tickets (reference). Unfortunately we are unable to resend them on your behalf, so adding another public comment to send a new outbound email will be required.

Root Cause Analysis

This incident was caused by United Internet applying an email block to mail sent from the broader zendesk.com domain. The intended scope of the block was limited to a single subdomain, following a high volume of email traffic from that source.

Because the block was applied at the broader domain level, it also affected legitimate ticket reply emails sent from other zendesk.com addresses.

Resolution

To resolve the issue, we submitted removal requests through the affected email providers’ support channels. United Internet then corrected the overly broad block. Outbound email delivery recovered, and SMTP 554 rejection responses stopped.

Remediation Items

  1. Develop a scalable process to identify and block abusive email activity more quickly.
  2. Define a controlled approach for gradually increasing outbound email volumes for new or high-volume customers.
  3. Introduce outbound email sending limits for new and trial accounts to reduce the risk of excessive sending activity.
  4. Improve customer self-service options for recovering ticket reply emails that are permanently rejected.

FOR MORE INFORMATION

For current system status information about Zendesk and specific impacts to your account, visit our system status page. If you have additional questions about this incident, contact Zendesk customer support.

articles.name: Configuring outbound queue selection in Contact Center
articles.title: Configuring outbound queue selection in Contact Center
articles.body:
Outbound queue selection lets agents choose the queue from which they place an outbound call. The selected queue determines the phone number displayed to the recipient and the Amazon Connect flow that handles the call.

What's my plan?
Add-on Contact Center

Summary: ◀▼

You can let agents choose an outbound queue for calls, which controls the caller ID shown to recipients and the flow that handles the call. You can allow access to all queues or only queues tied to the agent’s routing profile. This helps you manage outbound call routing and queue selection, but calls from queues without an outbound number will fail.

Location: Contact Center > Routing > Outbound calls.

Outbound queue selection lets agents choose the queue from which they place an outbound call. The selected queue determines the phone number displayed to the recipient and the Amazon Connect flow that handles the call.

For information about configuring routing profiles and their queues, see Updating Amazon Connect routing profiles for Contact Center. For the agent procedure, see Selecting the outbound queue for a call.

To turn on outbound queue selection

  1. In Contact Center, click Routing > Outbound calls.

  2. Select Allow agents to select an outbound queue.
  3. Select the queues that agents can access:
    • All queues: Agents can place a call from any queue, regardless of their Amazon Connect routing profile.
    • All queues associated with the agent's routing profile: Agents can place a call only from queues associated with their Amazon Connect routing profile.
    Note: Queues appear to agents even if they don't have an outbound number. Calls placed using those queues fail.
  4. Click Save.

    Agents can now select one of the available queues when placing an outbound call.

articles.name: Updating Amazon Connect routing profiles for Contact Center
articles.title: Updating Amazon Connect routing profiles for Contact Center
articles.body:
A routing profile in Amazon Connect defines the queues that agents can handle, the priority and delay for each queue, and the maximum number of simultaneous contacts. It also sets the default outbound queue for agent-initiated calls.

What's my plan?
Add-on Contact Center

Summary: ◀▼

You can update an Amazon Connect routing profile to control which queues agents handle, set queue priority and delay, and limit concurrent contacts. This helps you manage agent capacity and set the default outbound queue for agent-initiated calls. If you turn on outbound queue selection, agents can choose an outbound queue for calls.

A routing profile in Amazon Connect defines the queues that agents can handle, the priority and delay for each queue, and the maximum number of simultaneous contacts. It also sets the default outbound queue for agent-initiated calls.

Each agent has one routing profile. To let agents choose an outbound queue, turn on outbound queue selection in Contact Center. For more information, see Configuring outbound queue selection in Contact Center.

For more information about creating routing profiles and linking queues to agents, see Create a routing profile in Amazon Connect to link queues to agents in the AWS documentation.

To update a routing profile

  1. In Amazon Connect, click Users > Routing profiles.
  2. Click the routing profile you want to edit.
  3. Update the channels, queues, and concurrency settings as needed.

  4. Click Save.

articles.name: Error: Zendesk Support could not be loaded due to an error
articles.title: Error: Zendesk Support could not be loaded due to an error
articles.body:
Issue symptoms

When I try to sign in to Zendesk, I see the error: Zendesk Support could not be loaded due to an error.

In the browser console and network logs, I may see 5xx errors.

Resolution steps

Antivirus or VPN tools can block access to required Zendesk resources and cause this error. Confirm whether affected agents still see the error when they connect from a device that doesn’t use these tools.

If users still have issues, contact Zendesk Customer Support and include an HTTP Archive (HAR) file from one affected user.

Why do I see "Zendesk Support could not be loaded due to an error"? How do I fix "Zendesk Support could not be loaded due to an error" when signing in? What causes "Zendesk Support could not be loaded due to an error"?

Antivirus or VPN tools can block access to required Zendesk resources and cause 5xx errors in browser console and network logs.

To resolve this error, follow these steps:

  1. Connect to your Zendesk help desk or ticketing system from a device that does not use VPN or antivirus tools.
  2. Check if the error disappears.
  3. If you still see the error, contact Zendesk Customer Support.
  4. Provide an HTTP Archive (HAR) file from an affected support person or agent.

articles.name: Service Incident - September 17, 2026 - Voice | Elevated Average Active Sessions on shard cluster 20.7 / sharddb-20-07 in Pod 20
articles.title: Service Incident - September 17, 2026 - Voice | Elevated Average Active Sessions on shard cluster 20.7 / sharddb-20-07 in Pod 20
articles.body:
Summary

Between 14:26 UTC and 17:40 UTC on 17 September 2026, Voice customers on Pod 20 experienced an issue that caused some agents to remain in wrap-up mode after calls. Affected agents were not offered new incoming calls, which could delay inbound call handling.

Timeline

September 17, 2026 16:53 UTC | September 17, 2026 9:53 AM PT

We are aware of an issue affecting Voice on Pod 20 that is causing agents to experience difficulties leaving wrap-up mode. We are also seeing some call recordings not appended to tickets as expected. We are investigating and will provide further information when we have a substantive update to share. In the meantime, we recommend trying to manually click "finish wrap-up" (don't wait for the auto-timeout), and in case "finish wrap-up" doesn't respond, toggle Voice availability Off then On. Please let us know if the issue persists after attempting the workaround. Thank you for your patience in the meantime.

September 17, 2026 18:25 UTC | September 17, 2026 11:25 AM PT

Our team has addressed the underlying cause of the issue that prevented some agents from exiting wrap-up mode after a Voice call.  Agents ending a call should see wrap-up, and all relevant agent availability functions are back to normal. Thank you for your patience while we recovered from this incident.

Root Cause Analysis

This incident was caused by a high volume of duplicate agent availability updates generated by a single Voice session. Because the service did not adequately prevent duplicate requests or limit repeated updates from an individual agent, the traffic overwhelmed shared processing capacity on Pod 20 and delayed lower-priority work.

Resolution

To resolve the issue, we temporarily disabled the affected account’s embedded calling feature to stop further repeated availability updates. We then allowed pending work to be processed and re-enabled the feature after system performance had stabilized.

Remediation Items

  1. Introduce limits on how frequently an individual user can submit availability updates.
  2. Add a controlled way to immediately pause embedded calling updates when abnormal activity is detected.
  3. Separate availability checks from the primary system responsible for saving updates, reducing pressure on critical services.
  4. Apply stricter safeguards to prevent excessive or repeated availability changes from being processed.
  5. Prioritize the work required to return agents to an available state after a call, reducing the likelihood of delayed incoming call handling.

FOR MORE INFORMATION

For current system status information about Zendesk and specific impacts to your account, visit our system status page. If you have additional questions about this incident, contact Zendesk customer support.

articles.name: Announcing the general availability of employee service AI agents
articles.title: Announcing the general availability of employee service AI agents
articles.body:
Zendesk is excited to announce the general availability of employee service AI agents, which are purpose-built to help organizations support employees across IT, HR, Legal, Finance, and other internal service teams.

This announcement includes the following topics:

  • What is changing?
  • Why is Zendesk making this change?
  • What do I need to do?

What is changing?

Employee service AI agents will become generally available to all eligible customers during the rollout period. Employee service AI agents provide AI-powered support in the help center, Slack, and Microsoft Teams; can connect to and leverage content from to 20+ enterprise knowledge sources while still respecting access permissions to the content; and support advanced action flows.

New functionality in this release includes:

  • Conversational support in the help center, Slack, and Microsoft Teams.
  • More than 20 knowledge connectors, such as Google Drive, SharePoint, Confluence, Notion, Slack, Teams, Box, and more.
  • Resource-level permissions for connected content.
  • Automatic deployment of a default AI agent for each brand for immediate time-to-value delivery, with the ability for admins to create additional custom agents.
  • Auto-escalation to human agents when necessary through the Create ticket action.
  • More actions in AI agents, which allow admins to connect the AI agent to workflows built in advanced action flows, so employee service AI agents can execute multi-system tasks and resolve requests end-to-end.

Beginning November 3, 2026, all eligible accounts will include a number of automated resolutions for each employee service AI agent per month. After an employee service AI agent provides the allowed number of automated resolutions, it pauses until the limit resets the following month or additional automated resolutions are purchased at $0.99 per resolution. The following plan-based limits apply:

  • Growth and Professional plans: 10 automated resolutions per employee service AI agent per month
  • Enterprise and Enterprise Plus plans: 15 automated resolutions per employee service AI agent per month

To purchase additional automated resolutions for employee service AI agents, use the Subscriptions page in Admin Center or contact your Zendesk account representative.

Why is Zendesk making this change?

The information needed to support employees is often spread across multiple systems, which can make it difficult for employees to find the information they need and slows down the teams supporting employees. Employee service AI agents are designed to bring knowledge and workflow automation into the channels employees already use, such as Slack and Microsoft Teams. They help organizations improve request resolution times, reduce repetitive work, provide permission-aware answers, and automate complex multi-step tasks across business systems.

What do I need to do?

Employee service AI agents are being rolled out to Employee Service Suite Growth plans and above as well as Customer Service Suite accounts that use Zendesk for employee services. If you're on a Customer Service Suite plan and want to opt out, contact Zendesk Customer Support or your Zendesk account representative prior to the rollout start date.

To start using employee service AI agents, see About employee service AI agents and Creating and deploying employee service AI agents. 

If you have feedback or questions related to this announcement, visit our community forum where we collect and manage customer product feedback. For general assistance with your Zendesk products, contact Zendesk Customer Support.

articles.name: I am trying to deploy to far more than 50 organizations with AI agents
articles.title: I am trying to deploy to far more than 50 organizations with AI agents
articles.body:
Issue symptoms

I am trying to deploy to far more than 50 organizations with AI agents. My company provides customer support for other organizations. Because of this, I use 1 web crawler per organization that I support.

The problem is there is a limit of 50 web crawlers for each AI agent. I am trying to deploy to far more than 50 organizations, but we are unable to import any knowledge from said organizations due to the limit on web crawlers. Do you have advice on a workaround or re-architecting this build with best practices?

Resolution steps

Firstly, the web crawler does not have a limit for each AI agent, but for each Zendesk account.

  • Consider reaching out to your sales team at Zendesk to ask for an alternative.

In addition, if your team has developer and engineering resources, you may be interested to make use of the Federated Search API concept and these 2 methods:

  • The Web crawler lets your team implement federated search in your help center without developer resources. Set up multiple crawlers in your help center search settings to crawl and index different content in the same or different websites.
  • The Federated Search API allows developers to build custom integrations and ingest external content records into your Zendesk search indexes. This API requires your developers to build and maintain a middleware layer and integrate the site that hosts the external content with the help center. External records ingested through the Federated Search API refresh based on your configuration, whereas web crawlers run based on your selected refresh schedule (daily, weekly, monthly, or never) or can be triggered manually.

articles.name: Knowledge sources don't pull CSV knowledge I uploaded
articles.title: Knowledge sources don't pull CSV knowledge I uploaded
articles.body:
Issue symptoms

I am using CSV knowledge and AI agents - Advanced (legacy). After installing the CSV Knowledge Importer, I can't get the AI Agent to pull from my CSV knowledge. No matter what question I am asking the AI agents for information from the CSV knowledge source, my bot simply goes to the default reply.

This is what I've done:

  • I have installed and added the CSV knowledge importer.
  • I have ensured the CSV knowledge is added as a knowledge source in AI Agents.
  • I then tried to ask the bot a very simple question from something I knew was in the CSV knowledge source.

Root cause

The Knowledge Reply use case may be restricted to articles from a Recommendation search rule.

Resolution steps

To solve this issue:

  1. Remove any Recommendation search restriction from your use case
  2. Ensure your Intent shows Generative replies > Response generated
  3. Publish your updated configuration
  4. Refresh the page or clear your cache and cookies, and the Knowledge sources should return replies

articles.name: Service Incident - September 16, 2026 - Support | Multiple Pods - Custom ticket status are deactivated and unable to reactivate issue
articles.title: Service Incident - September 16, 2026 - Support | Multiple Pods - Custom ticket status are deactivated and unable to reactivate issue
articles.body:
Summary

On September 16, 2026, from 09:00 UTC to 12:20 UTC, Support customers on multiple pods experienced an issue that caused custom ticket statuses to appear inactive or become unavailable. As a result, agents were unable to use or reactivate these statuses, disrupting routine ticket updates, macro execution, and related workflows until service was restored.

Timeline

September 16, 2026 11:14 UTC | September 16, 2026 4:14 AM PT

We are aware of an issue affecting custom ticket statuses. Some customers may see statuses marked as inactive and be unable to restore them, while other statuses may not appear at all. Our engineering team has identified the cause and is actively working to resolve the issue. We apologize for the disruption and will provide another update as soon as more information is available.

September 16, 2026 11:32 UTC | September 16, 2026 4:32 AM PT

We have deployed a fix for the issue affecting custom ticket statuses. Please check whether your statuses are now visible and can be managed as expected. If you still see missing or inactive statuses, please reply to let us know. We will be happy to continue investigating with you. We apologize for the disruption and appreciate your help in confirming the resolution.

September 16, 2026 12:13 UTC | September 16, 2026 5:13 AM PT

Our engineering team is continuing to roll out the fix for the custom ticket status issue to the remaining affected service environments. We appreciate your patience while this work is completed and will provide further updates as they become available.

September 16, 2026 12:41 UTC | September 16, 2026 5:41 AM PT

Our engineering teams have completed deployment of the fix. Please verify whether custom ticket statuses are now displaying and functioning as expected. If the issue persists, please clear your browser cache and cookies, then check the ticket statuses again using a private or incognito browser window. If the issue continues after these steps, please contact us so we can provide further assistance.

September 16, 2026 14:18 UTC | September 16, 2026 7:18 AM PT

We are happy to report that the issue affecting custom ticket statuses has been resolved. Thank you for your patience during our investigation.

Root Cause Analysis

This incident was caused by a production code change that removed a required setting used to determine whether custom ticket statuses were enabled. As a result, the system treated the feature as unavailable, causing custom ticket statuses to appear inactive or missing for affected customers.

Resolution

To resolve the issue, we halted the affected deployment and reverted the change that removed the required custom ticket status capability. We then performed controlled recovery actions to restore all affected Classic environments to the expected software version.

Remediation Items

  1. Add checks before and after updates to confirm custom ticket statuses continue working as expected.
  2. Improve the process for reversing updates so that service can be restored more reliably if an issue occurs.
  3. Make feature availability more consistent when product changes are introduced.
  4. Add additional safeguards to protect customer-facing features from being unintentionally affected by updates.
  5. Improve and standardize how service updates are published, ensuring communications are timely and consistent.

FOR MORE INFORMATION

For current system status information about Zendesk and specific impacts to your account, visit our system status page. If you have additional questions about this incident, contact Zendesk customer support.

These notification settings work for usage tracked by the Automated resolutions dashboard as well as usage tracked by the Resolution allowance and Resolution usage dashboards. See Managing usage notifications for automated resolutions and resolution allowances. 

  • If you have the resolution allowance pricing model, you can increase your resolution allowance to cover ticket resolutions and avoid hitting usage limits. Account owners and billing admins with eligible accounts can increase the resolution allowance directly from the Subscription page or from the Resolution allowance dashboard. The added funds act as a shared pool across resolution tiers. See Increasing your resolution allowance.

Support

  • You can now turn on a multi-recipient email ticket workflow that creates multiple tickets when an inbound email with multiple support addresses is sent to the same account. See Turning on multi-recipient email tickets.
  • Sender authentication now defaults to Minimal for all accounts, raising security while improving legitimate email delivery. Existing customers can keep managing or disable authentication in Admin Center, and eligible disabled accounts will be rolled into the new default during a staged rollout. See Authenticating incoming email (SPF, DKIM, DMARC, and ARC).
  • Ticket merge enhancements update the merge flow with a sidebar drawer, richer text support, better bulk-merge visibility, hover context, colored status indicators, banner warnings, and preserved Data Privacy restrictions. See Merging tickets.
  • Admins on non-Enterprise plans now manage light agent permissions on the Roles page in Admin Center, replacing the previous settings experience in the Agent Workspace. See Configuring light agent permissions.

  • Agents working with a large numbers of ticket tabs, can use a singe command to close all tabs in the ticket interface. Previously, if agents wanted to clear all the tabs to make space for new incoming work, they needed to clear each tab one at a time. See Closing all tabs at once. 

  • Agents can adjust the sound volume for in-product notifications and personalize it for their own use. See Managing ticket notification settings. 

Admin Center

  • Admin Center search has been improved to provide better results. Search includes better discoverability across navigation and settings pages and more relevant results for incomplete or imperfect queries. See Searching for settings in Admin Center. 

AI agents

  • Voice AI agents are now generally available for Zendesk voice customers, enabling native end-to-end phone automation with real-time conversations, seamless handoff to human agents, transcripts, summaries, recordings, and support for 53 languages. See About voice AI agents.
  • Embedded templates are now available for email AI agents with agentic AI, letting admins send verbatim messages and use deterministic conditional or integration logic inside generative procedures. No action is required unless you want to customize templates. See Creating and using templates in conversation flows for AI agents.
  • Segments in procedures now work for email AI agents. You can use segments to send different customers down different paths, adapting a generative procedure's behavior to the customer. For example, a single "Cancel subscription" procedure can offer a retention discount to standard customers, while routing enterprise customers to their account manager. See Using segments to create branching conditions in generative procedures for AI agents.
  • Redaction in AI agent tickets is now possible. You can redact sensitive information from AI agent tickets, giving you the same data privacy controls for AI agent conversations that you have for regular tickets. Manual redaction and redaction suggestions now work on AI agent tickets.
  • A migration tool for essential AI agents is now available. When you use the AI agent migration tool on an essential AI agent, a new AI agent is automatically created for you in the new AI agent experience. The new AI agent replicates the functionality of your existing AI agent. See Migrating essential AI agents to the new unified AI agent experience using the migration tool.
  • The new “Ask for details” block in the dialogue builder allows AI agents to collect structured information from customers during conversations. This block acts as a configurable data collection form, allowing admins to define specific fields that the AI agent should gather before proceeding with the conversation flow. See Using the "Ask for details" block in dialogues for AI agent conversations.
  • A Welcome reply for email AI agents is now available. It allows for pre-conversation logic (such as conditionals based on parameters or segments, actions, API integrations, or escalations) to run before the AI agent takes over the email conversation. See Customizing the welcome reply in AI agent conversations.
  • A Knowledge reply for email AI agents is now available. The AI agent uses this reply when no relevant use case is detected. It searches your connected knowledge sources to generate an answer in the same way as any other generative procedure, in the same place you configure the rest of your AI agent. See Customizing the Knowledge reply in an AI agent with agentic AI.

Copilot

  • Saved recommendations are now available in admin copilot, letting you save useful recommendations for later and revisit them from a dedicated tab in Admin Center. See Optimizing your account with admin copilot insights and recommendations.

  • Draft mode for auto assist procedures lets you save, test, and manage procedure updates in Knowledge admin without changing live agent suggestions. You can also restore previous versions if needed. See Viewing procedure revisions.
  • Auto assist procedures list search is now available in Knowledge admin, allowing you to quickly search Copilot procedures instead of scrolling through long lists. This improves retrieval and management for accounts with many procedures. See Viewing and managing procedures for auto assist.

Objects and business rules

  • Automated data sync for custom objects now lets admins schedule Salesforce data synchronization into Zendesk custom objects, using AI-suggested field mappings, preview testing, daily runs, manual jobs, and sync logs. See Creating data sync schedules for custom objects.
  • Action logs and tracing for action flows give admins real-time visibility into action runs, with 30 days of run history, filtering, and step-by-step trace details to diagnose failures faster. See Monitoring real-time action flow execution logs and traces.
  • Action Builder workflow limits are increasing from 50 to 60 steps across all supported plans, letting you build longer, more detailed automated workflows. Existing action flows remain unaffected, and no action is required. See Understanding the action builder and action flows.
  • Wait steps make it possible to pause action flows for 1 minute to 31 days before continuing. This simplifies delays, escalations, follow-ups, and other multi-stage workflows, with wait details captured in execution logs. See Adding wait steps to action flows.
  • Cloning action flows and steps allow you use existing action flows as a starting point for new flows and copy and paste individual steps into other action flows. Both of these features help teams reuse configurations, save time, and reduce setup errors for action flows. See Editing and managing action flows.

Security

  • Accounts with session inactivity timeouts of 10 hours or more will migrate to an 8-hour inactivity timeout for enhanced security. All existing long-running sessions exceeding 12 hours will be forcibly expired, requiring a new sign-in. See Setting session timeout for users.

Knowledge

  • Universal Connector is now generally available as a knowledge source, letting admins connect REST/JSON API-based content to Zendesk with an API key and configure mapping, pagination, and retrieval for use in AI agents, Copilot, search, and generative search. See Connecting external content using the universal knowledge connector.
  • Helpjuice, WordPress, and ReadMe knowledge sources are now generally available as dedicated Zendesk connectors, letting admins sync external content into Zendesk Knowledge for use in AI agents, Copilot, search, and generative search. See Connecting external knowledge sources to your Zendesk account.

Messaging

  • Streaming animation now makes AI agent responses in the messaging Web Widget appear as if they’re being typed in real time, creating a more natural and responsive experience.
  • WhatsApp re-engagement adds 24-hour reply window visibility in the Agent Workspace, lets agents browse, preview, and send approved templates after the window closes, and gives admins a new WhatsApp templates page to manage template access in Admin Center. See Applying WhatsApp templates in the Agent Workspace.
  • Multi-conversations are on by default for new customers. Existing customers and their current messaging configuration will not be changed or migrated. See Allowing multiple conversations for your end users.

Contact Center

  • Outbound user search allows agents to find Zendesk users by name or phone number and place outbound calls directly, while still supporting manual keypad dialing. See Making outbound calls in Contact Center.
  • Outbound queue selection helps agents choose the appropriate caller ID and call flow for each outbound call. This gives agents more flexibility while helping teams route calls consistently. See Selecting the outbound queue for a call.
  • Voicemail lets callers leave messages when agents are unavailable, queues are busy, or the center is closed, and automatically creates or updates Zendesk tickets with caller details, audio, routing information, and optional transcription. Your deployment owner must upgrade your stack to version 1.2.8 (20260908) or later. Zendesk admins can configure voicemail for each queue, including ticket routing, tags, and transcription. See Configuring voicemail in Contact Center.

Voice

  • Voice AI agents are now generally available for Zendesk voice customers, enabling native end-to-end phone automation with real-time conversations, seamless handoff to human agents, transcripts, summaries, recordings, and support for 53 languages. See About voice AI agents.

Employee services

  • The IT asset records list now supports customizable columns, advanced filtering, and sorting by standard or custom asset fields, making it easier for admins and agents to find and organize assets. See Filtering and searching for asset records and Configuring the columns of the asset record list.

  • Automated IT asset data syncs now let IT admins automatically sync device and asset data from Jamf Pro and Microsoft Intune into Zendesk, with logging, retry, cancellation, and import-type options for better visibility and larger data sets. See Creating automated data syncs for assets and custom objects.
  • Custom roles and department spaces are now available to Employee Service Suite Professional plans, giving admins more control over permissions and ticket access without needing an Enterprise plan. See Custom roles and Restricting agent ticket access by brand: department spaces.

  • Approval request comments in Slack now let approvers reply directly in Slack, with comments synced to Zendesk as an auditable record. Comments are labeled via Slack or via Zendesk. Admins must reconnect Slack and enable approval requests to use the feature.

Workforce management

  • Forecast scenario imports are now generally available in Zendesk WFM, letting you upload CSVs with inbound volume forecasts or both forecasted volume and required staffing. This helps you use your own planning data and reduce manual reconciliation. See Importing forecast scenarios.

  • Workstream inbound volume CSV exports are now available in Zendesk WFM, letting admins self-serve a 30-day CSV of ticket IDs that entered a workstream. The export is requested from the workstream setup page and emailed for quick, auditable reconciliation. See Exporting a workstream’s inbound volume.

  • Team members permissions in Zendesk WFM now give admins granular control over who can access and manage the Team members page. They can let non-admin managers view scoped users and manage team, workstream, task lock, and auto-tracking assignments without granting full Admin access. See WFM permissions.

  • Simplified schedule imports in Zendesk WFM. You can now import agent schedules into Zendesk WFM using a simplified CSV file. Include the agent, intraday variant, start time, and date, and WFM generates the corresponding shift automatically instead of requiring you to define each task individually. See Importing and exporting your WFM schedules.

Quality assurance

  • AutoQA tone calculation changes. To improve accuracy and ensure Zendesk QA’s AI capabilities align with the highest regulatory standards, we are proactively updating the Tone category. See Understanding autoscoring categories .
  • Zendesk QA audit logs. QA now records review, scorecard and workspace events in Zendesk Admin Center audit logs. See Viewing Zendesk QA change events in the audit log.

  • Accuracy scores for custom prompts now appear in a new column. The column shows the AI insight’s accuracy score based on a comparison between autoscores and all manual reviews completed for that prompt. See Accessing the AI Insights page.

Apps and integrations

  • New Google Sheets actions in action flows make it possible to search for matching data, read specific rows, update rows, and insert rows, making it easier to manage spreadsheets and automate workflows without leaving Zendesk. See Using Google Sheets actions in action flows.
  • WooCommerce connections and actions are now available for action builder. You can use the WooCommerce actions to automate ecommerce support workflows, including creating, updating, looking up, and searching for customers, orders, and products. See Using WooCommerce actions in action flows.
  • New actions for BambooHR and Shopify make it possible to manage BambooHR custom tables and fields, as well as Shopify orders, customers, products, return eligibility, and legal policies, enabling more complete HR and ecommerce automations through action flows. See Using BambooHR actions in action flows and Using Shopify actions in action flows.
  • Smartsheet connections and actions are now available for action builder. You can use Smartsheet actions to automate management of Smartsheet sheets, rows, and project processes to add, find, update, and organize support-related work. See Using Smarsheet actions in action flows.
  • ShipStation and AfterShip connections and actions are now available for action builder. You can automate shipping, tracking, orders, and returns workflows, allowing admins to build more consistent post-purchase support workflows. See Using ShipStation actions in action flows and Using AfterShip actions in action flows.

articles.name: Using Intercom actions in action flows
articles.title: Using Intercom actions in action flows
articles.body:
Before you can include external actions in your action flows, you must connect the action builder to the external system.

What's my plan?
All Suites Team, Growth, Professional, Enterprise, or Enterprise Plus
Support Team, Professional, or Enterprise

Summary: ◀▼

Connect action flows to Intercom to automate support tasks across platforms. After you authorize the connection with an access token, you can create, look up, and update contacts and conversations, create tickets, search conversations, and list admins, help articles, and companies. Use a dedicated service account and review permissions before connecting.

By connecting the action builder to external systems, such as Intercom, admins can integrate Zendesk with external systems in automated workflows, improving collaboration and maintaining a seamless experience across multiple platforms.
Note: The steps associated with external systems in action flows are referred to collectively as external actions.
This article contains the following topics:
  • Connecting Intercom to action builder
  • Using Intercom actions in action flows

Connecting Intercom to action builder

Before you can include external actions in your action flows, you must connect the action builder to the external system.

When connecting to external systems for use in action flows, the following best practices are recommended:
  • All external actions performed by an action flow are attributed to the user who connected the external system. Therefore, it's a best practice to use a dedicated service account rather than personal credentials when connecting to each external system.
  • All integrations request access to necessary scopes. However, it's important that you review and validate the scopes before authorizing the connection to the external system.
  • When managing credentials for API key-based tools, such as OpenAI, it's best to store keys in a secure vault or credential manager.

The Intercom connection requires an access token with the following permissions: Read and write access to contacts, conversations, tickets, companies, and admins in your Intercom workspace.

You can generate an access token in your Intercom account by going to Developer Hub > your app > Authentication > Access Token.

Important: Review the permissions carefully before authorizing the connection. The access token allows action flows to perform operations on your behalf.
To connect action builder to Intercom
  1. In Admin Center, click Apps and integrations in the sidebar, then select Actions > Action flows.
  2. Create or edit an action flow.
  3. Open the step sidebar.
  4. Under External actions, click Intercom.
  5. Click Connect.
  6. Follow Intercom's prompts to enter your Intercom API key and complete the connection.
    Note: All external actions performed by an action flow are attributed to the user who connected the external system. Therefore, it is a best practice to use a dedicated service account rather than personal credentials when connecting to each external system.

After you've connected to the system, you'll see an indicator that it's connected and details about the instance you're connected to, as well as the actions available for Intercom.

Using Intercom actions in action flows

The following Intercom actions are available:
  • Create contact
  • Lookup contact
  • Create conversation
  • Lookup conversation
  • Reply to conversation
  • Create ticket
  • Search conversations
  • List admins
  • List help articles
  • List companies

Creating a contact

Use the Create contact action to create a new contact (user or lead) in Intercom.

This action has the following inputs and outputs:

  Variables
Inputs Optional: External ID, Email, Email verified, Phone, Name, Avatar URL, Role, Signed up at, Owner, Unsubscribed from emails; custom attribute fields are dynamically generated based on the workspace's contact custom attributes
Output Contact details including ID, external ID, email, name, role, phone, avatar, owner, location, tags, companies, notes, subscription preferences, and activity timestamps.

Looking up a contact

Use the Lookup contact action to retrieve Intercom contact details by ID or email.

This action has the following inputs and outputs:

  Variables
Inputs Optional: Contact ID, Email (provide either one, not both)
Output Contact details including ID, external ID, email, name, role, phone, avatar, owner, location, tags, companies, notes, subscription preferences, and activity timestamps.

Creating a conversation

Use the Create conversation action to initiate a new Intercom conversation (handoff or live chat) with a contact.

This action has the following inputs and outputs:

  Variables
Inputs Required: From (the contact initiating the conversation, with type and contact ID), Message body

Optional: Subject, Attachment URLs (comma-separated, up to 10), Created at (YYYY-MM-DD), Brand ID
Output Message details including message type, message ID, created date, subject, body, message type (email/inapp/facebook/twitter), and conversation ID.

Looking up a conversation

Use the Lookup conversation action to fetch a single Intercom conversation with its full message history.

This action has the following inputs and outputs:

  Variables
Inputs Required: Conversation ID

Optional: Display as (Plain text or HTML)
Output Conversation details including ID, source, contacts, teammates, assignee, state, read status, tags, priority, SLA, statistics, and the full message history.

Replying to a conversation

Use the Reply to conversation action to add a reply message to an existing Intercom conversation.

This action has the following inputs and outputs:

  Variables
Inputs Required: Conversation ID, Message type (comment visible to customer or internal note), Sender type (admin or user), Reply body

Optional: Admin ID (required when sender type is Admin), Contact ID (required when sender type is User), Attachment URLs (comma-separated, up to 10), Created at (YYYY-MM-DD)
Output Reply details including part type, body, author, attachments, and creation, update, and notification timestamps.

Creating a ticket

Use the Create ticket action to create a new Intercom ticket from a customer request.

This action has the following inputs and outputs:

  Variables
Inputs Required: Ticket type, Contact (provide contact ID, external ID, or email)

Optional: Conversation to link, Company ID, Created at (YYYY-MM-DD), Admin assignee, Team assignee, Title, Description, Skip notifications; ticket attribute fields are dynamically generated based on the selected ticket type.
Output Ticket details including ticket ID, display ID, category, ticket type, ticket state, associated contacts, assignees, ticket attributes, open and shared status, and linked conversations and tickets.

Searching conversations

Use the Search conversations action to find Intercom conversations matching search criteria.

This action has the following inputs and outputs:

  Variables
Inputs

Required: Search conditions (combine conditions with AND/OR)

Optional: Results per page (1-150), Starting after cursor (from the previous response, for pagination)
Output Paginated list of conversations matching the search criteria, including total count, pagination details, and full conversation details with message history.

Listing admins

Use the List admins action to list all admins and agents in the Intercom workspace.

This action has the following inputs and outputs:

  Variables
Inputs Optional: Display avatar (include admin avatar image URLs in the response)
Output List of admins including IDs, names, emails, avatars, team IDs, away mode settings, and inbox seat status.

Listing help articles

Use the List help articles action to retrieve all help center articles from Intercom.

This action has the following inputs and outputs:

  Variables
Inputs None
Output Paginated list of help center articles including IDs, titles, descriptions, bodies, authors, states, and URLs, with total article count and pagination details.

Listing companies

Use the List companies action to retrieve a list of companies from Intercom.

This action has the following inputs and outputs:

  Variables
Inputs Optional: Page, Per page (1-150), Sort order (ascending or descending by last request date)
Output Paginated list of companies including IDs, names, plans, monthly spend, session and user counts, size, website, industry, custom attributes, tags, segments, and notes.

Auto Assist Procedure Recommendations and Management

Apps and integrations

    • Zoom WFM opens from the Zendesk top bar with a compact agent experience built for Zendesk. Agents can view their schedule and handle time off, schedule change, and swap requests without leaving the agent workspace. If your account enables it, agents can also access the schedule offer board directly in Zendesk. Relevant Workforce Management alerts appear as native Zendesk notifications, helping agents stay informed in one place.   • DataSpeak Agent Assist (Support)
    • DataSpeak helps organizations answer questions faster, guide agents with reliable knowledge, and keep every conversation consistent with their brand voice — without losing control of workflows or data. DataSpeak brings your AI assistant into Zendesk Agent Workspace so agents get help without leaving the ticket.  Once connected, agents can chat with your DataSpeak assistant in the ticket sidebar, new ticket sidebar, user sidebar, and nav bar; get ticket-aware answers with subject, status, requester details, and related context passed into the conversation; summarize tickets, search Help Center knowledge, and draft clearer replies without switching tools; resume or thread chats per ticket via secure conversation references; and optionally identify the signed-in Zendesk agent in DataSpeak 
  • Super Search (Support)
    • Search tickets, macros, triggers, automations and more—all in one workspace. Super Search brings tickets, users and organizations together with searchable catalogs of macros, triggers, automations and webhooks, helping you find records and explore the configuration behind your support workflows. Super Search combines record search, configuration catalogs and per-ticket audit evidence in a navigation-bar workspace. 
  • Access Controller (Support)
    • LaPlante Management built Access Controller to help Zendesk teams protect important values from accidental edits, simplify crowded workspaces, and replace scattered field-ID lists with readable access profiles. Create an All agents baseline; build reusable profiles for Groups, Roles, or individual Agents; set supported fields and tag editors to Editable, Read-only, or Hide; set ticket forms to Editable or Hide; control individual Type, Priority, and eligible custom dropdown choices; vary field and choice rules by ticket form, brand, assigned group, or new/existing state; inspect an agent's matching profiles and compare effective access before saving; duplicate profiles and apply confirmed bulk changes; and open web addresses from read-only fields in a new browser tab. 
  • Similar Tickets (Support)
    • Similar Tickets brings useful ticket history into the conversation an agent is already handling. It searches the current Zendesk account, ranks related conversations, and displays the strongest matches directly in the ticket sidebar. Agents can review how similar incidents, questions, and customer issues were handled without leaving the ticket or guessing which search terms to use. 
  • Dual Frame (Support)
    • Designed by LaPlante Management, Dual Frame brings shared website bookmarks and embedded tools into Zendesk. Give agents one organized menu for reference pages, tools and reporting links, with no iframe code to write. Place bookmarks in full navigation, beside tickets or in a top-menu pop-up. Reuse them across locations and tailor menus to agent groups. 
  • Change Management (Support)
    • Change Management adds an ITIL change practice to Zendesk Support, running on native Zendesk tickets, forms, triggers, and approvals. Changes move from draft through assessment, CAB approval, scheduling, implementation, and post-implementation review to closure, with required fields enforced at each step. Impact and likelihood score change risk against a rubric your administrators control. A change calendar, collision detection for overlapping windows, and configurable freeze periods show what else is scheduled before you commit.
  • Incident Management (Support)
    • Incident Management adds an ITIL incident practice to Zendesk Support, running on native Zendesk tickets, forms, triggers, and approvals. Impact and urgency set Zendesk priority automatically through a matrix your administrators control. Major incidents unlock declaration, communication, and running update fields, along with a list of linked child incidents and a one-click way to raise the remediation change. Recurring pattern detection spots repeat incidents and can open a problem record with those incidents already linked to it.
  • Request Management (Support)
    • Request Management adds a service request practice to Zendesk Support, running on native Zendesk tickets, forms, triggers, and approvals. Requests move from submission through approval and fulfillment to closure, capturing catalog item, justification, and due date. Approval is routed to a person or a group through Zendesk's own approvals, so the decision and who made it stay on the ticket record. Work cannot begin until the request is approved, and fulfillment notes are required before it can be marked fulfilled.
  • Problem Management (Support)
    • Problem Management adds an ITIL problem practice to Zendesk Support, running on native Zendesk tickets, forms, triggers, and approvals. Problems move from open through investigation and known error to resolution, capturing root cause, workaround, RCA method, and permanent fix. Linked incidents are gathered from both Zendesk relationship types, and a similar-incident search lets you attach related incidents in bulk. Resolving a problem resolves its open incidents and records on each one why it was closed.

  • Admin Center
  • Support
  • Copilot
  • Analytics
  • Zendesk Workforce Management (WFM)
  • Mobile SDKs
